title: Fake News Detection: Comparative Evaluation of BERT-like Models and Large Language Models with Generative AI-Annotated Data

live_model.evidence: Sec. 6: "we utilized GPT-4 Turbo as an annotator, which precluded its use as a classifier in our experiments" (explaining why it was not evaluated as a classifier)

prompt.note: Figure 2 illustrates the two-shot annotation prompt used to label the dataset, not a classifier-evaluation prompt; GPT-4 Turbo was never run as a classifier.

claim.metric: none for the live id (GPT-4 Turbo used only to annotate the 10,000-article dataset; explicitly excluded from the classifier comparison)

data.source: 10,000 articles from Google RSS feeds, GPT-4 Turbo-annotated and human-reviewed (Sec. 3.1.2, 4.1); not released as a public downloadable dataset per the paper's data availability statement

notes: GPT-4 Turbo's only role is two-shot annotation of the 10,000-article fake/real news dataset (Fig. 2), later verified by humans. The paper explicitly states (Sec. 6) it excluded GPT-4 Turbo, Claude, and GPT-3.5/4 from the classifier comparison because GPT-4 Turbo had been used as the annotator, so there is no classifier-role number to reproduce.
